commonErrors.example: A learner writes on the worksheet that tails must be more likely after three heads because it is overdue.

fixIt.corrected: Corrected working: the coin has no memory, so the next toss is still 1/2 tails.
fixIt.prompt: Fix it: state the probability of tails on the next toss of a fair coin and say what the coin remembers.

commonErrors.misconception: After three heads, tails is due.

commonErrors.example: On the exit ticket, a learner answers that the probability of tails after three heads is more than 1/2.

fixIt.corrected: Corrected check: each toss is independent, so P(tails) stays at 1/2 however long the run of heads.
fixIt.prompt: Fix it: choose the correct probability for tails after a run of heads and give the reason.

commonErrors.misconception: After three heads, tails is due.

modelAnswers.question: A bag contains 5 counters, 3 of them red. Write P(red) as a fraction, a decimal and a percentage.
A coin is tossed twice. List all four outcomes in the possibility table.

nextSteps: Reteach the trap, landing that the coin has no memory: the next toss is still 1/2.
Practise the check from the worked example - P(red) and P(blue) sum to 1 because exactly one colour must come out.
strengths: Most of the class can calculate P(event) as favourable over total and write the same value as a fraction, a decimal and a percentage.
The class can build the two-toss possibility table with one outcome per cell and multiply along the branches.
